risk_reasons: The change alters connection scheduling for every postgres.js client in Vercel and Railway.
A regression can starve request or worker database access, while an incomplete fix leaves the permanent active/ClientRead Connection wedge possible.
goal: Concurrent database work beyond a postgres.js pool's connection count queues client-side instead of pipelining onto busy connections, preventing the Connection wedge across overlapping Fluid Compute requests.
non_goals: Move additional read call sites from sql to sqlRead.
Undo the per-request sequentialization shipped by issues 761, 767, and 779.
Deploy to staging or production, mutate remote data, or change remote environment variables in this review-ready run.
user_visible_behavior: Concurrent dashboard and admin renders complete without creating postgres.js pipelining wedges when aggregate demand exceeds the local connection count.
Excess database work waits for a connection, so overload appears as bounded request latency rather than a permanently leaked pool slot.
invariants: The existing max connection budgets, idle timeout, lifetime, connect timeout, and statement timeouts remain unchanged.
All production postgres.js clients inherit one central max_pipeline=1 policy.
The health-bundle differential retains an explicit max_pipeline=100 negative control that can still reproduce the historical wedge on an ephemeral branch.
No query, schema, tenant scope, authorization, or durable data contract changes.
edge_cases: Two or more overlapping requests can collectively exceed a pool even when each request stays below it; the queueing policy applies at the isolate-wide client.
A single request can also exceed the pool; it queues rather than pipelines.
Dedicated clients used by worker pollers inherit the safe policy unless the checked-in differential explicitly requests the historical pipeline depth.
If a future postgres.js version stops accepting max_pipeline, the parsed-client option tests fail rather than silently restoring the default depth of 100.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/db/server.ts BASE_POSTGRES_OPTIONS as the single owner of pinned postgres.js connection behavior.
src/lib/db/__tests__/server.test.ts assertions against postgres.js's parsed client options.
scripts/health-bundle-differential.ts branch-isolated negative-control and cure-arm experiment.
test_seams: The exported sql and sqlRead parsed options.
health-bundle-differential run-arm configuration and evaluateRun verdict.
tests_to_add: all production postgres.js clients cap max_pipeline at one
createDedicatedPostgresClient permits an explicit legacy pipeline depth for the differential only
concurrent max-two with max_pipeline one is a required clean cure arm
a wedged max_pipeline-one arm fails the differential as a cure regression
rollback_plan: Revert the central max_pipeline option and its differential cure arm, then redeploy the previous artifact. The change writes no data and requires no data rollback; the prior per-request sequentialization remains in place during rollback.
observability: During the ephemeral-branch differential, concurrent-max2 with the historical pipeline depth wedges while concurrent-max2 with max_pipeline=1 fulfills with zero active/ClientRead signature backends.
During the staging Vercel soak, all response bodies complete within the accepted latency bound and pg_stat_activity shows zero aging active/ClientRead wedge signatures.
Backend and Supavisor client connection peaks remain within ADR 0009's measured ceilings because pool maxima are unchanged.
